executive_summary: The shop's resilience is compromised by several critical weaknesses. A hidden coupling between astronomy-db and checkout causes checkout latency breaches even when not predicted, making checkout vulnerable to unrelated service slowdowns. The cart service itself is a single point of failure; its crash aborts all cart journeys. Front-end components (frontend, frontend-proxy, product-catalog) amplify tiny delays into system-wide outages, showing an overly broad blast radius. Additionally, the valkey-cart cache and flagd service expose hidden dependencies that can cascade failures to the cart. Add

weaknesses.title: Hidden checkout dependency
weaknesses.explanation: Delays on astronomy-db repeatedly breach the checkout latency threshold (>800 ms) even though checkout was not in the predicted journey map, indicating an undocumented coupling that can degrade checkout performance across all user flows.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-143142-3011, exp-163723-5939, exp-141736-9801, exp-165933-0066 all show checkout p95 >800 ms, impact 1.00, breadth 1.00, penalty 82-66.

fix.fix_title: Add timeout and retry to checkout calls to astronomy-db
fix.steps: Wrap all calls from checkout service to astronomy-db with a client library that sets a 200 ms timeout and retries up to 2 times with exponential backoff. Log fallback latency. This isolates checkout from transient DB delays.
fix.expected_effect: Checkout latency stays under 800 ms even when astronomy-db experiences 100-300 ms delays.

weaknesses.title: Cart service single point of failure
weaknesses.explanation: A crash of the cart service aborts all cart-related journeys, causing a full-impact outage (impact 1.00) despite a limited blast radius, revealing the cart as a critical single point of failure.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-142250-d200 crash on cart, impact 1.00, breadth 0.25, recovery 6.01 s, penalty 60.

fix.fix_title: Run cart service with replica and restart
fix.steps: Update docker-compose to define two replicas of cart service and set restart: unless-stopped. Use deploy.resources limits to ensure each replica gets sufficient CPU/memory.
fix.compose_override:
services:
  cart:
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '0.5'
          memory: 512M
fix.expected_effect: Cart crash affects only one replica; other continues serving, eliminating full-outage.

weaknesses.title: Broad blast radius from frontend delays
weaknesses.explanation: Small latency injections (100 ms) on frontend-related services trigger watchdog breaches across all major journeys, showing that latency in these front-door components propagates system-wide.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-141542-f9bb (frontend), exp-164224-dcfe (product-catalog), exp-170022-0d38 (frontend-proxy) each have impact 1.00, breadth 1.00 (or 0.75), penalty ≥53.

fix.fix_title: Circuit breaker on frontend entry points
fix.steps: Introduce a circuit-breaker middleware in frontend and frontend-proxy that opens after 3 consecutive >100 ms responses, returning a cached fallback page. Include retry with short back-off for product-catalog calls.
fix.expected_effect: Latency spikes in entry services no longer cascade, keeping overall journeys within thresholds.

weaknesses.title: Valkey-cart cache single point
weaknesses.explanation: Crashing the in-memory cache degrades the cart journey to the maximum impact, indicating that loss of the cache cannot be tolerated without severe user-experience degradation.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-104221-fd4f crash on valkey-cart, impact 1.00, breadth 0.25, recovery 6.01 s, penalty 60.

fix.fix_title: Add replica and fallback for valkey-cart
fix.steps: Deploy two instances of valkey-cart with restart: unless-stopped. Configure cart service to fall back to persistent DB if both caches miss or are unavailable.
fix.compose_override:
services:
  valkey-cart:
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '0.3'
          memory: 256M
fix.expected_effect: Cache crash no longer degrades cart journey; cart continues using DB fallback.

weaknesses.title: Flagd hidden cart dependency
weaknesses.explanation: A crash of flagd, though refuted, still shows an undocumented dependency on the cart service, causing cart latency spikes and highlighting hidden coupling that could surface under real failures.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-141616-6842 crash on flagd, hidden dependency on cart, impact 1.00, breadth 0.25, penalty 60.

fix.fix_title: Feature flag client with timeout and fallback
fix.steps: Wrap flagd client in cart service with a 150 ms timeout and default flag values. On timeout or error, use cached defaults to avoid latency spikes.
fix.expected_effect: Flagd failure does not propagate latency to cart, removing hidden coupling impact.

formula: penalty = 100 x (0.5 x impact + 0.3 x breadth + 0.2 x recovery); service score = 100 - worst penalty on that service; overall = mean of service scores weighted by the number of journeys the service sits on (at least 1; the larger of the map's count and the journeys it was seen to degrade).
methodology: An independent synthetic prober exercises four user journeys (home, product, cart, checkout) through the front proxy every second. It is the ground truth and does not depend on the application's own telemetry.

A baseline run fixes per-journey error rate and p95 latency and derives safety thresholds from them. A watchdog aborts any experiment that breaches a threshold or loses sight of the prober. Before injection, the safety agent reviews the plan against the baseline limits, recent outcomes and the learned limits, and may approve it, reduce its intensity or veto it; it can never raise an intensity. The planner remembers, across runs, the lowest intensity per target and fault kind that the watchdog or safety agent aborted, and does not propose that intensity or a higher one again within the lookback window. An advisory safety agent re-checks the live measurements every few seconds and may abort earlier; it can never cancel a watchdog abort, extend a fault or change a threshold.

Each experiment injects one fault (container crash, added network delay or packet loss), measures every journey during the fault window (up to the abort for aborted runs), reverts the fault, and measures how long the journeys take to return inside the baseline band.

Impact, breadth, recovery and the penalty are computed deterministically from those measurements. The hypothesis verdict compares the journeys the planner predicted would degrade with those that actually did: CONFIRMED when equal, PARTIAL when they overlap, REFUTED when they do not.
A hidden dependency is a journey that degraded by at least 0.3 although neither the hypothesis nor the dependency map expected it.

The analyst agent ranks weaknesses and the fixer agent proposes fixes from the measured results only; their output is validated against known experiments, services and an allowlist of compose keys. When Groq is unavailable or its output is invalid, rule-based fallbacks produce the same sections. Fixes are proposals and are never applied.
